items.title: Performance errors in video laryngoscopy
items.summary: A taxonomy of the specific ways a hyperangulated blade goes wrong, named by mechanism rather than by outcome.

_homepage.note: This is the companion to the Kovacs sign entry the feed carried earlier in the month: a glottis filling more than half the screen means the blade has gone too deep and over-rotated, and the correction is to withdraw and de-rotate even though it costs you the pretty view. The underlying point is that maximal glottic exposure and favourable geometry for tube delivery are not the same thing, which is the error most people never learn they are making. Read it before a shift where you expect a difficult airway rather than after one.

items.title: Ambient AI Scribes and Emergency Department Documentation Burden
items.summary: 10,344 encounters, 73 seconds saved per patient — a real effect, and far smaller than any vendor pitch.

_homepage.note: The adjusted 28 per cent reduction in on-shift documentation time is one of very few ambient-scribe figures drawn from a cohort large enough to adjust for confounding, which makes it the right thing to hold against the single-arm ACEM-journal study this feed carried, where 7.1 hours of saving was modelled rather than measured. A separate comparison of roughly 198,000 encounters found human scribes still ahead of AI, 3.3 minutes against 1.6, with no difference in clinical productivity either way. If this lands in a Victorian department, the honest claim is less typing after a shift, not more patients through it.

items.title: Catheter-directed thrombolysis works
items.summary: PRAGUE-26 cut the seven-day composite from 6.8 per cent to 0.7 per cent, and Farkas argues the real barrier was never the evidence.

_homepage.note: Farkas's framing is that catheter-directed thrombolysis is simply low-dose alteplase delivered into the pulmonary arteries, and that the hesitation is psychological — giving tPA to someone who might have done fine on heparin alone. The Czech trial randomised 558 patients across eleven centres and reported no deaths in the intervention arm against four in standard care, using plain 4-French infusion catheters, since SUNSET already showed ultrasound facilitation adds nothing. Worth reading before the ESC pulmonary embolism guideline revision, because this is the trial it will turn on.

items.title: WHO opens the third Ebola emergency committee on the DRC
items.summary: Over 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths across eight provinces, and the committee has now convened three times without lifting the emergency.

_homepage.note: The number that matters here is not the case count but the more than 1,000 contacts lost to follow-up, because that is what predicts where this goes next. Tedros also cites an attack that killed 66 civilians including three health workers — the reason tracing is failing is security rather than epidemiology. The feed has carried the individual DON bulletins and the Kenya 42-day countdown; this is the governance layer sitting above them, and the first place a change in the PHEIC status would show.

items.title: ECM Records: A primer for dedicated listening
items.summary: A label primer written to be read with the records on, which is a different thing from a buyer's guide.

_homepage.note: The shelf already runs to Oscar Peterson, Stan Getz and the Milt Jackson and Ray Charles sessions, and ECM is the obvious adjacent direction from there — same seriousness about recorded space, a completely different aesthetic. ISC builds these primers for its dedicated listening hours and hands them out as take-home guides with label, personnel and context, modelled on Chee Shimizu's Tokyo sessions. It is a reading list for an evening rather than something to skim.

items.title: Hermanos Gutierrez Turn the Andes Into a Cinematic Soundscape
items.summary: The seventh record trades the American West for the charango and Peruvian percussion, with Dan Auerbach producing.

_homepage.note: Both ends of this record are already in the collection — Hermanos Gutierrez on one side, the Black Keys on the other, and it was Auerbach who cut it at Easy Eye Sound in Nashville. The departure is Alejandro picking up the charango on 'Canto Andino' and 'Ciudad Inca', and 'Tren Macho' being built on the rhythm of a historic Peruvian railway rather than the desert reverb the duo is known for. Reviewers broadly agree it is their most rooted album and a shade less distinctive for it, which is a reasonable trade.

items.title: Why Does Colour Negative Film Have an Orange Mask?
items.summary: No dye is perfect, and the mask exists to cancel the errors — which is why a scanner inversion is doing more work than it looks.

_homepage.note: This is the piece that explains why an uncorrected C-41 scan looks the way it does, and why Kodak Aerocolor IV — increasingly repackaged and sold as cheap colour stock — behaves differently, because it carries no mask at all. Useful if rolls are being scanned at home rather than handed over, since the inversion step is exactly where the mask comes off and where colour goes wrong. 35mmc has been the most productive photography source in this feed and this is one of its better technical explainers rather than another camera report.

items.title: 5 Frames With Belomo Etyud
items.summary: A Soviet plastic box with a viewfinder the author calls close to unusable, returning negatives far better than it has any right to.

_homepage.note: The verdict is the whole argument for cheap Soviet glass in one sentence: the camera is awkward to aim and the pictures come back better than expected. Five Frames is the format where the photographs carry the piece rather than the spec sheet, which is the right way round for this brief — the topic is the pictures, not the kit. Worth a look if the Pentax 17 end of the market has started to feel like the only way back into film.

items.title: Dragonwilds Adds Earth Magic Ahead of December's Luminance Update
items.summary: Earth is the fourth element and it is a defensive school, not another damage option — the first real combat addition since 1.0.

_homepage.note: Earth Runes go on staves and wands from Magic 14, the staff special drops an earthquake with aftershocks, and landing hits stacks Armour of the Earth up to three — so the reason to switch is survivability rather than throughput. Update 1.0.2, 'Eye on Ashenfall', also brings a Killer Gentoo Penguin hunt with its own shop, an Umbral Sands quest called A Reel Downer, and roughly thirty fixes. Jagex has started a PTR with a selected group of Steam players, and is holding elves, the Lyre and the Prayer skill for Luminance in December.

items.title: First Look: Waxflower Opens The Atrium in Brunswick
items.summary: The bar that started Melbourne's listening scene in 2021 has opened a much larger room next door, and you can bring your own records.

_homepage.note: The BYO DJ sets are the part that matters with 297 records sitting at home — Waxflower is at 153 Weston Street, just off Lygon, and co-owner Marek Polgar has described the place as a wine bar with an epic sound system. The Atrium is built for visual arts and events rather than simply more covers, so it is a different proposition from the original room rather than an extension of it. It is also the closest thing on the northside to the audiophile listening spaces In Sheep's Clothing keeps cataloguing.

items.title: Big pitfalls for tiny patients
items.summary: A paediatric resuscitation that comes apart through team roles and communication, not through any drug or dose.

_homepage.note: The failure mode is the one that actually happens in a mixed department: a team forms around a small child, nobody states who is doing what, and the errors follow from that rather than from a knowledge gap. Paediatrics sits adjacent to his case mix rather than inside it, but the crisis-resource-management half of this travels straight back into adult resus. Scenario-led and short, which makes it a reasonable thing to read before a paeds-heavy roster.

items.title: Why do my flannels keep wearing through?
items.summary: Crompton answers a reader who keeps blowing out flannel trousers, and the answer is not to buy heavier.

_homepage.note: The useful correction here is that ounce weight is a poor proxy for durability in flannel, because the nap is a finish rather than the cloth itself — so buying up does not reliably buy longer. He also rates moleskin as the only winter trouser he finds more comfortable than flannel, which is worth filing alongside the Woolrich and Pendleton end of the brief. Relevant to a Melbourne winter specifically, where the cloth is wanted but sixteen ounces of it is not.
